svg.title: Which findings in a child who has sickle cell disease should the nurse report as possible acute chest syndrome? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: Acute chest syndrome is the leading cause of death in sickle cell disease , so this list is reported immediately: chest, back or abdominal pain, fever 38.5 C or above , cough, tachypnea, dyspnea and wheeze. Isolated joint pain that settles with simple analgesia is an ordinary crisis, not this.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Clinical reasoning
Read the situation
Which findings in a child who has sickle
cell disease should the nurse report as
possible acute chest syndrome? Select all
that apply.
What fits here
Fever of 38.5 C (101.3 F) or higher ·
Cough · Wheezing · Tachypnea · Chest, back
or abdominal pain
Why it fits
Acute chest syndrome is the leading cause
of death in sickle cell disease , so this
list is reported immediately: chest, back
or abdominal pain, fever 38.5 C or above ,
cough, tachypnea, dyspnea and wheeze.
Isolated joint pain that settles with
simple analgesia is an ordinary crisis,
not this.
